nodes.summary: Kahn–Kalai–Linial inequality for events under the uniform measure (J. Kahn, G. Kalai, N. Linial, *The influence of variables on Boolean functions*, FOCS 1988), with constant `2`: `2 · P(A)(1 - P(A)) · log (1 / maxₑ Infₑ(A)) ≤ ∑ₑ Infₑ(A)`, where `Infₑ(A)` is the probability that `e` is pivotal for `A`.
nodes.title: Kahn–Kalai–Linial inequality

nodes.summary: The KKL inequality `KKLHypercontractive p 2` for an event: `2 · P_p(A)(1 - P_p(A)) · log (1 / maxₑ Infₑ(A)) ≤ ∑ₑ Infₑ(A)`.
nodes.title: KKL inequality with constant 2 at $p$ implies its event form

nodes.summary: `kklw_hkkl_of_hypercontractive` at every `p` in the interior of `[1/2, q]`.
nodes.title: KKL on the interior of $(1/2, q)$ implies its event form there

nodes.summary: `StatMech.BeffaraDC.influence` is the OSSS influence of the indicator of `A`.
nodes.title: Pivotal-probability influence as the OSSS influence of an indicator

nodes.summary: `log (1 / maxₑ Infₑ(A))` under the Bernoulli(`p`) product measure.
nodes.title: Logarithm of the reciprocal maximal influence of an event

nodes.summary: `StatMech.prob p A` is the OSSS expectation of the indicator of `A`.
nodes.title: Event probability as the OSSS expectation of its indicator

nodes.summary: Window form of `kklw_sharpThreshold`: under the same hypotheses, if `P_q(A) ≤ 1 - ε` then `q - 1/2 ≤ (1/2 - ε) / (2 v₀ L)`.
nodes.title: Sharp-threshold window bound assuming the KKL inequality on $(1/2, q)$

nodes.summary: Sharp-threshold bound: for an increasing event with `P_{1/2}(A) = 1/2`, if the KKL inequality holds for all `p ∈ (1/2, q)` and there `P_p(A)(1 - P_p(A)) ≥ v₀` and `log (1 / maxₑ Infₑ(A)) ≥ L`, then `P_q(A) ≥ 1/2 + 2 v₀ L (q - 1/2)`.
nodes.title: Sharp-threshold bound assuming the KKL inequality on $(1/2, q)$

nodes.summary: The variance of the indicator of `A` is `P(A)(1 - P(A))`.
nodes.title: Variance of an event indicator is $P(A)(1 - P(A))$

nodes.summary: The OSSS Bernoulli weight of a configuration is `StatMech.configWeight`.
nodes.title: OSSS Bernoulli weight equals the configuration weight

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
